claims.text: The proposed material is a refractory high-entropy alloy in the as-cast state.
The intervention is addition of 5 wt% tungsten to the alloy.
Adding 5 wt% tungsten will improve yield strength at 1000°C under tensile loading by 20% relative to the tungsten-free baseline.
The tungsten-modified alloy will have a density below 8.5 g/cm³.
The tungsten-modified alloy will retain room-temperature yield strength within 10% of the baseline value.
Tungsten addition will produce solid-solution strengthening.
Tungsten addition will cause precipitation of tungsten-rich phases.
Added tungsten will form a solid solution with the alloy's other elements.
Tungsten in solid solution will increase lattice distortion.
Increased lattice distortion will strengthen the alloy at high temperature.
Tungsten-rich precipitates will provide dispersion hardening.
The tungsten-free baseline alloy has a yield strength of 500 MPa at 1000°C.
A room-temperature yield-strength range of 450–550 MPa represents retention within 10% of the baseline.
The magnitude of the high-temperature improvement may depend on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions.
Precipitation of tungsten-rich phases may affect ductility and toughness.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a 20% high-temperature yield-strength improvement, but the experiment only falsifies improvements below 15%; a result between 15% and 20% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying it.
Room-temperature yield strength is required to remain within 10% of baseline, whereas the falsification rule permits deviations up to 15%.
